cast: The LORD God, who speaks the world into being and then walks in its garden in the cool of the day.
Adam and Eve, the first man and woman, placed in a garden with a single prohibition.
Noah, a righteous man told to build an ark of gopher wood before the waters come.
Moses, raised in Pharaoh's house and sent back to demand freedom for a people in bondage.
David, a shepherd's youngest son who carries bread and cheeses to his brothers at the battle line.
Job, a wealthy and upright man of the land of Uz, blameless and much blessed.

contentNotes: extensive warfare, massacre and the killing of civilians
slavery treated as ordinary and regulated
rape and other sexual violence
child sacrifice and killing of infants
detailed animal sacrifice and butchery
executions, stonings and mutilation
plague, famine and mass death

cast: Alice, a curious, literal-minded English girl who thinks a book without pictures is no use at all.
The White Rabbit, a fretful creature in a waistcoat who is always late and always running.
The Caterpillar, a hookah-smoking grump who answers every question with another question.
The Cheshire Cat, a grinning cat who appears, advises, and disappears whenever it likes.
The Hatter and the March Hare, hosts of a tea party that never gets tidied up.
The Queen of Hearts, a monarch whose response to almost everything is an order for beheading.

cast: Alice, a curious, polite and quietly argumentative seven-year-old who climbs through her drawing-room mirror.
The Red Queen, brisk and imperious, who sets Alice running and lays down the rules of the country.
The White Queen, untidy and anxious, forever losing combs and living her life the wrong way round.
Humpty Dumpty, an egg on a wall, magnificently certain that words mean exactly what he chooses.

John and Michael Darling, her younger brothers, one full of pirate lore, one still very small.
Mrs. Darling, whose mouth holds one kiss that nobody has ever managed to get.

Nana, a prim Newfoundland dog engaged as the children's nurse.

cast: The lion, strong, proud, and easily flattered
The fox, quick-witted and almost never honest

cast: Mr. Utterson, a dry, dependable London lawyer who would rather help a friend than judge him

cast: Dorothy: a plain-spoken Kansas farm girl carried a long way from a very grey home.
Toto: her small black dog, the one thing on the prairie that still plays.

cast: John Carter: a Virginian fighting man on Mars, faster and stronger there than any native swordsman.

a fatal staged carriage crash
threats, blackmail and corrupt police
an attempted assault with a raised hand and a drawn revolver
a casual antisemitic remark about a public figure
period condescension toward Americans

cast: Mark Ablett, the dapper, vain owner of the Red House, who always wants an audience
Matthew Cayley, his big, heavy-jawed cousin, who quietly runs everything for him
Antony Gillingham, an idle young man with £400 a year who collects odd jobs and odder people
Bill Beverley, a cheerful house guest in white flannels and Antony's friend
Audrey Stevens, the pretty parlour-maid who opens the door to the visitor

contentNotes: A man shot dead; the body is examined briefly but plainly

cast: Roberta, called Bobbie: the eldest, quick to notice when the grown-ups are unhappy and quicker to hide it.

contentNotes: a parent taken away and a family's abrupt fall into poverty
a near rail disaster and a child collapsing afterwards
a cabin fire with a baby inside, and a badly broken leg set at home
period talk about foreigners, and a man exiled to a Russian prison camp

Helen Fairclough: her steady friend, engaged to the missing Major Felstead.
Sir Henry Cranston: Philippa's husband, a retired naval man apparently content to fish and dine well.
Nora: the freckled stepdaughter, still in schoolroom plaits and thoroughly pleased with herself.
Captain Griffiths: the awkward, sallow Commandant who can never say what he means.
Hamar Lessingham: a courteous stranger who arrives by an extremely irregular route.

period anti-German feeling

cast: The narrator — a young wife and new mother, ordered to rest and forbidden to work or write
John — her husband and physician, affectionate, practical, and quite certain she is not really ill

Mary — the woman who minds the baby the narrator cannot bear to be near

contentNotes: depiction of mental breakdown
postpartum depression
a woman confined and medically controlled by her husband
a passing thought of jumping from a window

Mr Marshfield, a chilly scientist who studies people the way others study beetles

women described as belonging to a tolerated trade
drunkenness, opium and drugging

Ann of Oxford Street, a poor girl not yet sixteen who shares her last coins with him
A neglected child who has been living alone in an empty London house and is afraid of ghosts
The head-master and the guardian whose quarrel drives the boy to run away
An unnamed druggist near the Pantheon, remembered ever after as something more than mortal

A neglected child living alone in an empty house
Period racism, particularly a hostile caricature of an Asian traveller and of Asia generally
Nightmarish dream imagery of drowning faces and endless architecture

cast: Charles Darwin — a collector-obsessed boy who thought himself an ordinary pupil and could never master a language.
Dr. Robert Darwin — his formidable, kind-hearted physician father, capable of one crushing sentence.
Professor Henslow — the Cambridge botanist whose dinners and long walks quietly redirect a young man's life.

A shipboard quarrel in which slavery is defended
The death of a parent in childhood
Sustained and frank religious doubt

cast: Sherlock Holmes: a consulting detective who is unbearable when he has nothing to solve.
Dr. John Watson: the army surgeon who shares his rooms and tells the story.
Mary Morstan: a governess whose father vanished in London ten years ago.
Thaddeus Sholto: a jumpy, art-collecting recluse with an inherited secret.
Athelney Jones: a police inspector who much prefers his own theories.

contentNotes: Recreational drug use, described in detail
Murder and a violent chase
A racist caricature of an Andaman Islander
Colonial-era attitudes and language

cast: The narrator, an English envoy stuck in Flanders on a negotiation that keeps stalling
Peter Giles, his cheerful and generous Antwerp friend, who makes the introduction
Raphael Hythloday, a Portuguese philosopher-traveller who gave away his estate to see the world
Cardinal Morton, a shrewd, kindly churchman who enjoys testing the people who come to him

Bribery, assassination and mercenaries as accepted tools of war
Public whipping, and death penalties for adultery and repeat offences
Period contempt for friars and monks

William Legrand, a Huguenot gentleman fallen on hard times, living alone on a sand island and collecting insects

suicidal thoughts
a wife's death treated as an aesthetic event

Monsieur G, the Prefect of police, who calls anything past his understanding odd.
Roderick Usher, a boyhood friend whose letter begs for company he can barely explain.
Prince Prospero, a wealthy and fearless host with a taste for the bizarre.
Montresor, a courteous narrator who has quietly decided a friend must be punished.

live entombment and premature burial
alcoholism and violence toward a wife

A servant knocked down by his master and boxed on the ear by his mistress
Duelling talk and a spell in jail on a false charge
Period prejudice about Scots, servants, Methodists and 'savages'

cast: Achilles: the best fighter in the Greek army, quick to rage and certain that his worth has been slighted.

Enslavement of captured women and open discussion of them as prizes

A brief moment of feared self-harm in grief

Dr John Watson: his steady friend and chronicler, still willing to be dragged out of bed at midnight.

suicide discussed as a possibility

wartime hostility towards Germans

cast: Carruthers, a fastidious young Foreign Office clerk left behind in an empty London
Davies, an unpolished Oxford acquaintance who sails a tiny boat alone and loves it
The Dulcibella, a cramped, flat-bottomed seven-ton yacht that is very nearly a character
Bartels, a gentle Dutch skipper who watches over Davies like a father
Dollmann, the aloof owner of a smart barge-yacht among the islands

contentNotes: Serious peril at sea; a stranding in a gale

Period German-invasion anxiety and nationalist rhetoric
A brief antisemitic caricature of a shopkeeper

cast: The narrator: a pilgrim who joins the company at the Tabard and promises to set down each of them exactly as they seemed to him.

medieval antisemitism, notably in the Prioress's tale

drunkenness and blasphemous swearing

cast: The narrator: a French archaeologist wandering Andalusia with two shirts and a copy of Caesar, curious about everything and frightened of nothing.

Wilhelm, the patient friend who receives every letter and is never heard replying.

a sexual assault recounted secondhand
mental illness shown in period terms
firearms

a husband's contemptuous treatment of his wife
a mother separated from her children

Period antisemitic remarks by characters
